newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 CPI sparks T-bill demand, zloty rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 CPI sparks T-bill demand, zloty rise.

text.p: The zloty strenghtened against the currency basket as foreigners bought Polish T-bills after better than expected December's inflation data faded market speculation about a near-term rise in official interest rates.

Analysts said official rates would likely stay stable until the end of the first quarter after inflation fell to 18.5 percent in 1996, against expectations of a 18.8 percent rise and last year's consumer price growth of 21.6 percent.
"This is the moment to enter for foreign investors after inflation figures signalled that official interest rates should not rise," said Pawel Lopuszynski, dealer at PKO SA.
The Polish zloty closed at 3.42/3.38 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 3.40/3.37 percent.
It closed at 2.9095/05 to the dollar, down from 2.9010/20 on Tuesday and at 1.8215/25 to the mark, up from 1.8282/88.

Three-month T-bills eased 0.2 point at 19.70/19.30 percent in secondary trade against the last primary 13-week average yield of 19.47 percent, but dealers said tomorrow's trade should solidify the secondary market's direction.
"I would wait until tomorrow to see where the market's expectations are," said Maciej Kwiatkowski from Societe Generale in Warsaw.
